definition: node2vec is an algorithm to generate vector representations of nodes on a graph.
details: The node2vec framework learns low-dimensional representations for nodes in a graph through the use of random walks through a graph starting at a target node. It is useful for a variety of machine learning applications. node2vec follows the intuition that random walks through a graph can be treated like sentences in a corpus. Each node in a graph is treated like an individual word, and a random walk is treated as a sentence. By feeding these "sentences" into a skip-gram, or by using the continuous bag of words model, paths found by random walks can be treated as sentences, and traditional data-mining techniques for documents can be used. The algorithm generalizes prior work which is based on rigid notions of network neighborhoods, and argues that the added flexibility in exploring neighborhoods is the key to learning richer representations of nodes in graphs. The algorithm is considered one of the best graph classifiers.

explainer.lead: node2vec turns graph nodes into low-dimensional vectors so ordinary machine learning can operate on graph structure. It matters because graph data is everywhere and most ML models expect fixed-length vectors, not edges.

tiers.eli5: Imagine walking randomly around a neighbourhood and writing down each stop; places that keep showing up on the same walks must be related, so you describe each place by the company it keeps.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run biased random walks from each node, feed the resulting node sequences into a skip-gram model, and read off embeddings for tasks like link prediction or node classification. Pitfall: the random-walk and window settings encode which notion of neighbourhood you get, so using defaults across very different graphs often yields embeddings that mix communities you wanted separated.
tiers.paperLevel: Two parameters steer the walk: return and in-out, which bias whether it stays local or explores outward; sequences are then learned with skip-gram or continuous bag-of-words over a context window. Known limits: embeddings are transductive, so nodes unseen at training time get no vector, and results are sensitive to the walk hyperparameters.

explainer.example: On a social graph, many short walks that revisit a node's immediate friends push that node's vector close to its close circle; long exploratory walks instead place it near nodes in other communities.
